headline: Paired rollout schedules reduce reward noise, but do not guarantee better agent learning
summary: The Sep. 21 arXiv paper analyzes paired, event-keyed environment schedules for group-relative reinforcement learning of tool-using agents. Its theory shows that pairing removes the shared environment-noise component from sibling reward contrasts but can still increase gradient variance under some score geometries. In a registered study using one Qwen3.5-2B agent and three seeds per design, pairing improved noisy-test success under transient tool faults by 5.1 points but missed the registered learning-curve criterion; under grader flips, the learning-curve difference was small and uncertain. A finite probe found lower gradient covariance traces, but the result is limited to eight checkpoints from two trajectories and does not establish broad learning gains.
